svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.7.5.2 Resistance to Forced Entry for Swinging Doors
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.7.5.2 Resistance to Forced Entry for Swinging Doors
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.7 WINDOWS, DOORS AND SKYLIGHTS
Resistance to Forced Entry for Swinging Doors

g.text: PLAN AT THE LOCK, STRIKE SIDE
Strike screws run into solid wood

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Applies to swinging entrance doors to dwelling units, doors between
dwelling units and attached garages or other ancillary spaces, and doors
giving access directly or indirectly from a storage garage to a dwelling
unit
Not exterior doors to garages and other ancillary spaces.
Or: doors, frames and hardware at least Grade 10 in the Annex to ASTM
These need not conform to Sentences (3) to (7).
Wood doors: solid core or stile-and-rail, at least 45 mm thick
Stile-and-rail panels at least 19 mm (¾″) thick, total panel area not more than
half the door area.
Deadbolt: cylinder with no fewer than 5 pins, bolt throw at least 25 mm
Protected with a solid or hardened free-turning ring or beveled cylinder
housing. See Article 9.9.6.7.
Inactive leaf of double doors: heavy-duty bolts top and bottom,
engagement at least 15 mm (9/16″)
Hinges: into wood doors with wood screws at least 25 mm long, and into
wood frames so that at least 2 screws per hinge penetrate 30 mm (1 3/16″)
into solid wood
Metal doors and frames: machine screws not smaller than No. 10, at least 10 mm
long.
Deadbolt strikeplates: wood screws 30 mm into solid wood
Metal frames: machine screws not smaller than No. 8, at least 10 mm long.
Outswinging doors: hinges or pins so the door cannot be removed when
closed
Except storm or screen doors.
Solid blocking on both sides at lock height, between the jambs and the
framing
So the jambs resist spreading by force.
Drawn: a door in exposed framing; gold is the solid blocking. Plan inset not to scale.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.7.5.2. (page 9-27)
